about: Well-known methods with a standard definition. The standard-method miner matches each entry's names against a function's name, its docstring, and the imported names its body uses. Every entry is general knowledge; none comes from a task.

methods.definition: The sum of the values divided by their count; a weighted mean divides the weighted sum by the sum of the weights.
The mean squared deviation from the mean; the sample variance divides by n - 1, the population variance by n. The standard deviation is its square root.
The middle value of the sorted values; with an even count, the mean of the two middle values.
The value below which the stated fraction of the sorted sample falls, with a stated interpolation rule between order statistics.
The value minus the mean, divided by the standard deviation.
Pearson's r is the covariance divided by the product of the standard deviations; Spearman's rho is Pearson's r on ranks; Kendall's tau counts concordant minus discordant pairs.
The mean product of deviations from the two means; the sample form divides by n - 1.
The largest absolute difference between the two samples' empirical distribution functions, computed on the same variable in both samples.
The sum over cells of (observed - expected)^2 / expected, with degrees of freedom from the table's shape.
The difference of means over its standard error; Welch's form uses each sample's own variance and the Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.
The sum over shared bins of (current share - reference share) * ln(current share / reference share), with bins fixed from the reference and every value assigned a bin.
KL(P||Q) is the sum of p * log(p / q), asymmetric and nonnegative; Jensen-Shannon averages KL of each to the midpoint distribution.
The negative sum of p * log p over outcomes; cross entropy is the negative sum of p * log q.
The squared distance between kernel mean embeddings; the unbiased estimator excludes the diagonal terms of the within-sample kernel matrices and divides by n(n - 1) and m(m - 1).
Repeatedly draws samples with replacement (or permutes labels) from the data under the null and recomputes the statistic on independent draws, never comparing a sample with a subset of itself.
An interval that covers the parameter at the stated rate; the Wilson score interval for a proportion centers on (p + z^2/2n) / (1 + z^2/n).
A mean over a sliding window; the exponential form updates s = alpha * x + (1 - alpha) * s.
The mean of kernels centered on each sample point, scaled by the bandwidth so the estimate integrates to 1.
The coefficients that minimize the sum of squared residuals; ridge adds lambda times the squared norm of the coefficients.
The parameters that maximize the product of the model's densities over the observations, equivalently the sum of log densities.
Predict the state and covariance with the transition model, then correct them with the gain K = P H^T (H P H^T + R)^-1.
Similarity is the dot product divided by the product of the two norms; distance is 1 minus that similarity.
The square root of the sum of squared coordinate differences.
The sum of absolute coordinate differences.
The number of positions at which two equal-length sequences differ.
The minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions that turn one string into the other.
The size of the intersection divided by the size of the union; the distance is 1 minus that.
2r * asin(sqrt(sin^2(dlat/2) + cos(lat1) cos(lat2) sin^2(dlon/2))), with angles in radians.
sqrt((x - mu)^T S^-1 (x - mu)) with S the covariance matrix.
The minimum cost of moving one distribution's mass onto the other's; in one dimension, the integral of the absolute difference of the CDFs.
exp(-gamma * ||x - y||^2), computed between rows of the two inputs.
Divides each vector by its L2 norm so it has length 1; a zero vector has no direction and must be handled explicitly rather than divided by zero.
(x - min) / (max - min), with a constant input handled explicitly.
exp(x_i) / sum_j exp(x_j), computed after subtracting the maximum for numerical stability.
A state changes only after its entry condition holds for the entry count, and changes back only after its exit condition holds for the exit count, so one opposite sample doesn't flip it.
Tokens refill at a fixed rate up to a capacity; a request passes only when it can take a token.
The wait before retry k grows as base * factor^k up to a cap, usually with random jitter.
Halves a sorted interval each step, keeping the half that must contain the target, with inclusive or exclusive bounds used consistently.
Settles vertices in order of tentative distance from a priority queue, relaxing each outgoing edge; requires nonnegative weights.
Visits each vertex once, marking it visited when it is discovered; a topological order lists every vertex before its successors and fails on a cycle.
Each set has a representative root; find follows parents to the root, and union links one root under the other.
A bijection between vertex sets that preserves adjacency (and labels, where given); VF2 extends a partial mapping only with pairs that keep it feasible.
Orders elements by the key; a stable sort keeps equal keys in input order.
On a hit the entry becomes most recent; when full, the least recently used entry is evicted.
Windows are defined in event time by their size, slide, or gap; a watermark is the event time up to which input is taken as complete, advancing monotonically.
Keys and nodes hash onto one ring; a key belongs to the first node clockwise, so adding a node moves only the keys it takes over.
k hash functions set k bits per inserted item; a query reports present only when all k bits are set, so it has false positives but no false negatives.
Keeps the first k items, then replaces a random slot with item i (1-based) with probability k / i.
For i from n - 1 down to 1, swaps item i with a uniformly chosen item from 0 to i inclusive.
Steps against the gradient by the learning rate; Adam keeps bias-corrected first and second moment estimates.
x_{k+1} = x_k - f(x_k) / f'(x_k), stopping on a tolerance.
Classic RK4 combines four slope evaluations with weights 1/6, 1/3, 1/3, 1/6; forward Euler steps y + h f(t, y); backward Euler and BDF solve for the new value implicitly.
X_k = sum_n x_n exp(-2 pi i k n / N), with the stated normalization and the inverse's 1/N.
Between two known points, a + t (b - a) with t in [0, 1]; a spline matches values and derivatives at the knots.
The trapezoid rule sums h (f_i + f_{i+1}) / 2; Simpson's rule weights 1, 4, 2, ..., 4, 1 times h / 3 over an even number of intervals.
Factorizes the matrix (LU with pivoting, Cholesky for symmetric positive definite, QR by orthogonalization) and solves by substitution.
r = (1 - d)/N + d * sum over in-links of r_j / outdegree_j, with dangling nodes spreading their rank to every node.
Alternates assigning each point to its nearest centroid and moving each centroid to the mean of its points until assignments stop changing.
Precision is TP / (TP + FP), recall is TP / (TP + FN), F1 is their harmonic mean; ROC AUC is the probability a random positive outranks a random negative.
CRC-32 is the IEEE polynomial 0xEDB88320 (reflected) with initial value 0xFFFFFFFF and a final XOR with 0xFFFFFFFF.
Base64 maps each 3 bytes to 4 characters from the 64-symbol alphabet and pads the last group with '=' (URL-safe form uses '-' and '_').
Each byte becomes two hexadecimal digits, high nibble first.
UTF-8 encodes each code point in 1 to 4 bytes with continuation bytes 10xxxxxx; Unicode normalization forms compose or decompose canonically (NFC, NFD) or by compatibility (NFKC, NFKD).
Bytes outside the unreserved set are written as % followed by two hex digits; form encoding writes a space as '+'.
Fields are separated by commas and records by line breaks; a field containing a comma, quote, or line break is quoted, with an embedded quote doubled.
Each run of equal symbols becomes the symbol and its count.
Huffman builds a prefix code by repeatedly merging the two least frequent nodes; LZ77 and LZW replace repeats with back-references or dictionary codes.
HMAC is H((K xor opad) || H((K xor ipad) || m)) with the key padded or hashed to the block size; a digest compares in constant time.
A block cipher mode as specified: CBC chains each block with the previous ciphertext and needs padding and a random IV; GCM needs a unique nonce and verifies its tag before releasing plaintext.
Vigenere shifts each letter by the key letter at the same position, repeating the key; autokey extends the key with the plaintext itself.
Three base64url parts joined by dots; the signature covers header.payload and is verified with the algorithm the verifier expects, and exp and nbf are checked.
HTTP messages follow RFC 9110: methods keep their safety and idempotency, a conditional request compares validators, and a body is framed by Content-Length or chunked encoding, not both.
A connection opens with SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK; unacknowledged segments are retransmitted after a timeout; the window bounds unacknowledged data.
Applying the same request or message twice has the effect of applying it once; deduplication keys on a stable identity, not on arrival order.
A write-ahead log records a change durably before it is applied and replays committed records in order on recovery; MVCC readers see the versions committed before their snapshot.
A value commits once a majority quorum accepts it in the current term; a node votes at most once per term.
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH compared numerically part by part; a pre-release ranks below its release.
Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and times hh:mm:ss with an explicit offset or Z; arithmetic is done in UTC and converted for display.
Luhn doubles every second digit from the right, subtracts 9 from results over 9, and requires the sum to be divisible by 10.
Round half to even sends ties to the even neighbor; round half up sends ties away from zero; decimal amounts round in decimal, not binary floating point.
